We say $ S $ is a zero-sum sequence if the sum of the elements in $ S $ is the zero element of $ G $. For a positive integer $ t $, let $ \\mathtt{s}_{t\\exp(G)}(G) $ (respectively, $ \\mathtt{s}'_{t\\exp(G)}(G) $) denote the smallest integer $ \\ell $ such that every sequence (respectively, zero-sum sequence) $ S $ over $ G $ with $ |S|\\geq \\ell $ contains a zero-sum subsequence of length $ t\\exp(G) $.
